subject: Governing law & 'break-glass' process - HelixHealth MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@helixhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@helixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA / Order Form - governing law + emergency relief

Hi Grace,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA and order form earlier this week. Our legal team did a pass and attached a redline (Helix_MSA_Redline_v3.docx). Two items we want to flag for discussion before we move to signatures:

1) Governing law: Helix prefers California law (due to our internal compliance group and precedent with cloud vendors).
2) Emergency relief / injunctive relief carve: We want a clear path to an expedited temporary restraining order in California state or federal court when intellectual property or patient-safety data is at risk.

We recognize Redwood's standard arbitration clause but need assurance that provisional measures to preserve evidence or prevent immediate harm are available locally. Can you propose language that preserves our ability to seek temporary injunctive relief in CA while keeping arbitration for final disputes?

Separate note: we requested a short excerpt of your SOC2 in the portal; we included a PDF stub for reference.

Appreciate a quick sync — Jacob (copied) is our counsel who will join if needed.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Contracts, HelixHealth

Attachment: Helix_MSA_Redline_v3.docx (redline)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft MSA / Order Form - governing law + emergency relief

Maria —

Thanks, and appreciate the redline. Short answer: we can accommodate a provisional relief carve for jurisdiction where relief is sought, but we need narrowly tailored language so the arbitration agreement remains effective for merits. Proposed compromise below that has worked in other customers:

"Notwithstanding the arbitration clause, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo, prevent imminent harm, or protect intellectual property or confidential data; such requests shall not be deemed a waiver of the parties' agreement to arbitrate the merits of the dispute."

On governing law: Redwood's standard is New York (uniformity across our contracts and predictable commercial case law). If Helix requires California, we can accept California for governing law provided we include a forum neutralization clause that confirms arbitration seat remains neutral and that provisional relief in CA does not waive arbitration.

I'll loop in Legal to vet specific phraseology and flag any operational impacts for our compliance team. Can we align on a 30-minute call tomorrow morning PT?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOC2-Report-Excerpt.pdf (stub)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Helix redline — provisional relief / governing law (internal)

Team — forwarding Helix's redline note. Quick priorities before the call:

- Helix wants CA governing law and explicit local injunctive relief.
- Risk: if we accept CA governing law broadly, we introduce split-law complexity for our templates and could face unfavorable consumer/statutory claims.
- Proposed approach: accept governing law = California, but insert a clause that (1) preserves arbitration as seat-neutral; (2) explicitly allows provisional relief in any court where relief is sought (standard carve); (3) limit injunctive relief to narrowly defined categories (IP, data protection, critical availability incidents).

Please review the redline (attached) — I will propose a clean markup for Helix post-call. Also: Sean, please confirm whether our support/ops team can commit to a 24-hour break-glass notification SLA for high-severity incidents (they asked about injunctive relief tied to patient-safety).

Thanks,
Grace

Attachment: Helix_MSA_Redline_v3.docx (forwarded)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helix redline — provisional relief / governing law (internal)

Grace —

Ops can commit to a formal incident notification SLA: for P0 incidents impacting Helix production we will: (a) notify named Helix contacts within 60 minutes, (b) provide escalations to on-call infra within 2 hours, and (c) open a dedicated incident bridge. We can also provide a signed runbook excerpt that documents the break-glass escalation steps.

On provisional relief language, Legal should keep the carve narrow — we don't want to create a route for forum-shopping. Suggest adding a 14-day notice-and-cure where feasible (except where immediate relief is required to preserve patient safety or IP).

Sean
VP, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@helixhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jacob Lee <jakob.lee@helixhealth.com>, Contracts <contracts@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Governing law & 'break-glass' process - HelixHealth MSA/Order Form

Grace —

Thanks for the quick responses and the internal coordination. Jacob and I reviewed your proposed compromise language and Helix can accept the arbitration + provisional relief carve if we add two items:

1) A short statement that the right to seek provisional relief "shall include the ability to seek temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions in California state or federal court where necessary to protect patient safety or PHI."
2) A concrete runbook addendum and a one‑page attestation from Redwood that the break-glass notification process is in place; Helix counsel will use that attestation when preparing internal approvals.

If Redwood can provide the one-page runbook and approve the exact carve language below, we can finalize and proceed to DocuSign:

Proposed language to include in Section X (Dispute Resolution - Provisional Measures):
"Notwithstanding Section Y (Arbitration), either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo, prevent imminent harm, or protect intellectual property or protected health information (PHI). Such provisional relief shall include the ability to seek temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions in California state or federal court when necessary to protect patient safety or PHI. Seeking such provisional relief shall not constitute a waiver of the parties' agreement to arbitrate the merits of the dispute."

Let me know if that exact language is acceptable. If so, we'll incorporate and circulate for signature.

Best regards,
Maria Gomez
Head of Contracts, HelixHealth

Attachment: OrderForm_HLX-001.pdf (order form stub)
